newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn coalition may forego gold revaluation in 97.
newsitem.headline: Bonn coalition may forego gold revaluation in 97.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition is willing to forgo plans to revalue central bank gold and currency reserves in 1997 as originally planned, coalition sources said on Tuesday.

The coalition source told Reuters that sharp criticism of the plan to revalue the central bank reserves against the Bundesbank's will from parliamentary deputies from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) had prompted the change.

Abandoning the plan to revalue the assets will mean that there is another 10 billion mark hole in the 1997 budget, the source said. To fill that hole, the coalition parties are discussing privatisations, budget cuts and moderate tax increases.
Earlier, Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Tuesday they were on the way to coming to an agreement on revaluing gold and currency reserves.
The Bundesbank was strongly opposed to Bonn revaluing the assets in 1997, a step which could help Germany meet the criteria to qualify for EMU.
